summary: Nora's own container now has the host Docker socket mounted, so that she can launch the sandbox containers the artifact-building capability runs in.
details: This is a real widening of what her process can do on the host: access to that socket is, by Docker's own model, equivalent to control of the machine.
It was raised explicitly and ruled on rather than slipped in, and it is named in docker-compose.yml beside the mount itself.

The sandbox containers themselves are contained: each runs on a network of its own that reaches only the artifact service, never the database, the message transport or the object store, and each holds a short-lived credential that can write only its own artifact.
Nothing in the running process touches the socket while the artifact capability is switched off, which is how it ships.
limitations: The mount is present whether or not the capability is enabled; only the calls are gated.
